chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fuzayl ibn Yasar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I have refrained from trade and withheld from it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'And why is that? Is it weakness on your part? That is how your wealth goes away. Do not refrain from trade, and seek from the Grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims continue to engage in trade and business according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) corrects the misconception that abstaining from trade is a form of asceticism, clarifying that such withdrawal often stems from weakness or laziness rather than piety. He emphasizes that engaging in lawful commerce is a means of seeking sustenance from Allah’s bounty, aligning with the Shia scholarly view that trade is a virtuous act when free from deceit and usury. This guidance underscores the balance between spiritual devotion and economic participation in Islamic society.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Fuzayl Bin Yasaar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I had refrained from the business and have withheld from it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And why is that so? Are you crippled with? That is how your wealth goes away. Do not refrain from the business and seek from the Grace of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn’ Udhaynah from Fudayl ibn Yasar who has said the following:

“I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I have quit doing business and have withdrawn thereof.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Why is that, are you helpless? This is how your wealth goes away. You must not quit doing business. You must continue to seek favors from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.’”
